[[File:Sugihokowakenomikoto-jinja, otorii.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Otorii}}]]'''Sugihokowake no Mikoto Shrine'' is located in {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Tanaka. In {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. '''Kawazu Kinomiya Shrine'' (not ``Kawazu'') <ref>[https://sugihokowakenomikoto.jimdo.com/ Official site of Kawazu Kinomiya Shrine (Sugisawabetsu no Mikoto Shrine)]</ref><ref>[http://www.kawazu-onsen.com/sightseeing/25 Large camphor tree of Kawazu Kinomiya Shrine] - Kawazu Town Tourism Association</ref>.

It is in charge of '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himemiya Shrine}}''', which is compared to ``Sasahara Hime no Mikoto Shrine'', a Shikinai shrine.

== Company name ==
In ancient times, it was called ``Sawabetsu Myojin'', ``Kino (Great) Myojin'', ``Kinomiya (Great) Myojin'', ``Kino Shrine'', ``Kino Shrine'', and ``Kinosaki Myojin'', and even today it is commonly known as ``Kawazu Kinomiya Shrine''. It is said to be a shrine with {{ill|Kinomiya Faith|ja|キノミヤ信仰|qid=Q11296898}}, as it has passed down the ancient name of ``Kinomiya'' and ``Tori Shojin Sake Shojin'' (described later).

== Enshrined God ==
The main deity is ``Sugihokowake no Mikoto'', and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isotake no Mikoto}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sukuhikona no Mikoto}} are enshrined in {{ill|Aidono|ja|相殿|qid=Q135009883}}. In "{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}", it is listed as 1 dai, so it is thought that it was originally dedicated to Sugisubetsu no Mikoto. </ref>.

=== History ===According to the shrine's legend, it had been enshrined since ancient times, but was rebuilt in the {{ill|Wadō (era)|ar|وادو (حقبة)|de|Wadō (Ära)|es|Wadō|fa|وادو (دوره)|fr|Ère Wadō|ia|Wado|id|Wadō|ja|和銅|ko|와도|pt|Wadō (era)|ru|Вадо|simple|Wadō (era)|sr|Вадо (ера)|th|วาโด|tr|Wadō|uk|Вадо (ненґо)|zh|和銅|zh_yue|和銅|qid=Q1373026}} period (708 - 15), and was listed as a small shrine in the Engishiki Shinmyocho. The tree was estimated to be over 1,000 years old in the early {{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} period (first half of the 20th century), and was designated as a national {{ill|Natural monument|ar|نصب تذكاري طبيعي|ast|Monumentu natural|ba|Тәбиғәт ҡомартҡыһы|be|Помнікі прыроды|be_x_old|Помнік прыроды|bg|Природна забележителност|bs|Spomenik prirode|ca|Monument natural|cs|Přírodní památka|da|Naturmonument|de|Naturdenkmal|eo|Naturmemorindaĵo|es|Monumento natural|et|Loodusmälestis|eu|Monumentu natural|fa|یادمان طبیعی|fi|Luonnonmuistomerkki|fr|Monument naturel|gl|Monumento natural|hr|Spomenik prirode|hy|Բնության հուշարձան|id|Monumen alam|is|Náttúruvætti|it|Monumento naturale|ja|天然記念物|ka|ბუნების ძეგლი|kk|Табиғат ескерткіші|ko|천연기념물|lv|Dabas piemineklis|mk|Споменик на природата|nl|Natuurmonument|nn|Naturminne|no|Naturminne|pl|Pomnik przyrody|pt|Monumento natural|ro|Monument al naturii|ru|Памятник природы|sh|Spomenik prirode|sk|Prírodná pamiatka|sl|Naravni spomenik|sq|Monument natyror|sr|Споменик природе|sv|Naturminne|th|อนุสรณ์สถานทางธรรมชาติ|tr|Tabiat anıtı|uk|Пам'ятка природи|uz|Tabiat yodgorliklari|zh|自然紀念物|qid=Q23790}} in 1936|Q18649}}. Since ancient times, it has been called ``Kimiya-sama's great Kusu'' and has been worshiped as {{ill|Shinboku|fr|Shinboku|ja|神木|simple|Shinboku|sv|Shinboku|zh|神木 (神道)|qid=Q48743901}}. There were once seven large camphor trees in Kawazu, and until the mid-Meiji period they were called ``Nanaka Kae Nanakusu,'' but this is the only one that remains today. There is also a large camphor tree near the approach entrance and in front of the shrine to the right.

In addition, there is also {{ill|Kinomiya Shrine|ja|来宮神社|zh|來宮神社|qid=Q11523682}} in {{ill|Atami|ar|أتامي (شيزوكا)|arz|اتامى|azb|آتامی، شیزوئوکا|ce|Атами|ceb|Atami (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Atami (Šizuoka)|cy|Atami|de|Atami (Shizuoka)|es|Atami|et|Atami|eu|Atami|fa|آتامی، شیزوئوکا|fi|Atami|fr|Atami|gl|Atami|he|אטאמי|hy|Աթամի|id|Atami, Shizuoka|it|Atami|ja|熱海市|ko|아타미시|lt|Atamis|mg|Atami|ms|Atami, Shizuoka|mzn|آتامی، شیزوئوکا|nl|Atami|pl|Atami|pt|Atami|ro|Atami|ru|Атами|sv|Atami|tg|Атами|th|อาตามิ|tl|Atami|tr|Atami|tt|Атами|tum|Atami|uk|Атамі (Сідзуока)|ur|اٹامی|vi|Atami, Shizuoka|war|Atami, Shizuoka|zh|熱海市|zh_classical|熱海市|zh_min_nan|Atami-chhī|zh_yue|熱海|qid=Q653364}} in the northern part of {{ill|Izu Peninsula|ar|شبه جزيرة إزو|az|İzu yarımadası|be|Ідзу (паўвостраў)|bg|Идзу (полуостров)|ca|Península d'Izu|ceb|Izu Hantō|de|Izu-Halbinsel|eo|Duoninsulo Izu|es|Península de Izu|eu|Izu penintsula|fa|شبه‌جزیره ایزو|fi|Izun niemimaa|fr|Péninsule d'Izu|he|איזו (חצי אי)|id|Semenanjung Izu|it|Penisola di Izu|ja|伊豆半島|ko|이즈반도|lt|Idzu pusiasalis|mn|Изү хойг|nl|Izu (schiereiland)|pl|Izu (półwysep)|pt|Península de Izu|ru|Идзу (полуостров)|rue|Ізу (пувострув)|simple|Izu Peninsula|sl|Polotok Izu|sv|Izuhalvön|th|คาบสมุทรอิซุ|tr|Izu Yarımadası|uk|Ідзу (півострів)|vi|Bán đảo Izu|zh|伊豆半島|qid=Q822822}}. alink|Azu Sawaki Shrine's Large Kusu|Q60403026}} There is a famous camphor tree (also a natural monument), which is often called the same name as "Kimiya Shrine's Kusu", so it is easy to confuse it.

Doso Shrine, Uga Shrine, Inari Shrine, Tenjin Shrine, Mizu Shrine, Kumano Shrine, Kojima Shrine, Toshino Shrine, Hobutsuki Shrine, Ohgusu Shrine, Sa Shrine, Yama Shrine, Onagotsusa Shrine

== Festival ==
Sakeru Festival (December 17th) / Sake Festival (December 24th) - Between the two festivals (December 18th - 23rd) is called {{ill|Kawazu's Tori Shojin Sake Shojin|ja|河津の鳥精進酒精進|qid=Q11553983}}, and it is said that when Sugisabetsu no Mikoto, who was drunk in the area, was about to burn to death in a wild fire, he was saved thanks to a large flock of small birds carrying water from their wings and extinguishing the fire, so Sugisabetsu no Mikoto forbade him to drink alcohol and eat poultry and eggs.

== Company name ==
In ancient times, it was called ``Himemiya'' or ``Himemiya Daimyojin.''

== Enshrined God ==
Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine ({{jalink|Emperor Nintoku|Q3 13119|Osazaki no Mikoto) and Kageyama Shrine (Kageyama Myojin) were enshrined together<ref>Properly, it was enshrined at Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine, and the main deity was changed to Sasahara Hime no Mikoto. </ref>.

== History ==
Ritual artifacts thought to date back to the 4th century have been unearthed near the former shrine grounds (305 Sasahara Himamiya, Kawazu-machi, currently on the grounds of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawazu Town Minami Elementary School}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himemiya Kindergarten}}) ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Himemiya Ruins}}), and it appears that it has been worshiped as a {{ill|Ubusunagami|ja|産土神|ko|산토신|zh|產土神|qid=Q1392097}} since ancient times. It is listed as a small shrine in the ``Engishiki Shinmyocho'', and is described as ``Junior Fourth Rank Upper Sawarahime no Miko'' in the ``Izu Province Shinto Namecho''. According to the shrine's biography, the shrine had territory until around {{ill|Genki (era)|ckb|گێنکی (سەردەم)|fa|گنکی|fr|Ère Genki|ja|元亀|ko|겐키|ru|Гэнки (эра)|simple|Genki|sr|Генки|sv|Genki|tr|Genki|zh|元龜|qid=Q1145064}} (1570 - 73), but for the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|ckb|تێنشۆ (سەردەمی مۆمۆیاما)|fa|تنشو|fr|Ère Tenshō (Momoyama)|ja|天正|ko|덴쇼 (아즈치모모야마 시대)|ro|Era Tenshō (Momoyama)|ru|Тэнсё (Адзути-Момояма)|simple|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|sr|Теншо (Момојама период)|sv|Tenshō|tr|Tenshō (Momoyama)|zh|天正 (日本)|qid=Q1145058}} years (1573 - == Shrine building ==
The main shrine is one-span {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684}} on both the front and sides, with a {{ill|Wood shingle|bat_smg|Guonts|be|Гонта|be_x_old|Гонт|cs|Šindel|csb|Szkùdło|de|Schindel|eo|Ŝindo|es|Tejuela|et|Sindel|fi|Paanu|fr|Bardeau|hr|Šindra|hu|Fazsindely|ja|杮葺|lt|Malksna|mk|Шиндра|nl|Dakspaan|no|Takspon|pl|Gont|ro|Șindrilă|ru|Дранка|rue|Шынґель|sh|Šindra|sk|Šindeľ|sl|Skodla|sr|Шиндра|sv|Spån (byggmaterial)|tr|Çatı örtüsü|uk|Ґонт|qid=Q199388}} roof with a staggered gable and a kara gable on the eaves. It is a late {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Έντο|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|new|इदो काल|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} shrine building.

Along the way is the entrance to Himemiya Shrine.
